steps.title: Meet us at Clubsfest or Facultyfest
steps.body: We have a table at both events at the start of term.
steps.todo: confirm we run this every term

steps.title: Fill in the form
steps.body: It asks what you are interested in and how much time you have. A resume is optional, so first years do not feel like they need one, and there is no minimum GPA.
steps.todo: link the real application form, confirm the close date

steps.title: Interview with a subteam
steps.body: Every subteam runs its own interview, usually 30 minutes to an hour, about what you would want to work on.

steps.title: Start building
steps.body: You are on the team. First-term members shadow a build and take on one small deliverable.

faq.q: I have never built anything. Can I still join?
faq.a: Yes, and most of us started there. First-term members are paired with someone who has done the job before, and your first deliverable is deliberately small. The team exists to teach this.

faq.q: I am not in engineering. Is there a place for me?
faq.a: Yes. Operations is a full subteam: it runs sponsorship, the budget, and everything we do on campus. Commerce, communications, humanities and science students all sit on it. Payload also takes science students most years.

faq.q: How much time does it actually take?
faq.a: About six hours a week for most members, rising in the four weeks before a launch and dropping to almost nothing over exams. We plan around the academic term.

faq.q: Do I need to pay anything?
faq.todo: answer this: membership fee, travel costs to competition, and what the team covers

faq.q: Can I join partway through the year?
faq.a: Not usually. We hire during a set window each term, at Clubsfest and Facultyfest, rather than on a rolling basis. Email us and we will tell you honestly when the next one opens.

faq.q: What if I want to try a different subteam later?
faq.a: Normal, and encouraged. Plenty of people move once they have seen what the other subteams actually do.
